# Feature 1: Price relative to its overall mean (normalized price deviation)
# Captures whether a product is expensive or cheap relative to average
price_mean = df['price'].mean()
price_std = df['price'].std()
df['price_zscore'] = (df['price'] - price_mean) / (price_std + 1e-8)

# Feature 2: Price per product_id magnitude (price relative to product scale)
# Products with higher IDs might be newer/different category price sensitivity
df['price_per_log_product'] = df['price'] / (np.log1p(df['product_id']) + 1e-8)

# Feature 3: User-price interaction ratio
# Captures relative purchasing power / affinity signal
# Higher user_id with lower price may indicate different behavior
user_id_norm = (df['user_id'] - df['user_id'].mean()) / (df['user_id'].std() + 1e-8)
df['user_price_ratio'] = user_id_norm / (np.log1p(df['price']) + 1e-8)

# Feature 4: Category deviation signal
# How far the category_id deviates from its mean (normalized)
cat_mean = df['category_id'].mean()
cat_std = df['category_id'].std()
df['category_deviation'] = np.abs(df['category_id'] - cat_mean) / (cat_std + 1e-8)

# Feature 5: Price bucket interaction with log product
# Discretize price into quantile buckets then interact with log product_id
# Captures non-linear price tiers effect
df['price_quantile'] = pd.qcut(df['price'], q=10, labels=False, duplicates='drop')
df['price_bucket_x_log_product'] = df['price_quantile'].astype(float) * np.log1p(df['product_id'])
